preferred_language: The Subcontractor shall maintain the insurances required under this Contract until the later of completion of the Subcontractor's scope and expiry of the Warranty Period, and shall not be required to maintain insurance by reference to substantial performance of the Project or the requirements of the Head Contract.

title: Waiver of subrogation - statutory limits
where_to_look: Waiver of subrogation and cross-liability provisions.
required: Waiver of subrogation given only where the policy permits it, with statutory schemes expressly carved out.
fallback: Express carve-out for workers compensation and compulsory motor vehicle cover. Provide certificates of currency rather than certified copies of policies.
escalate_if: Agreeing a blanket waiver of subrogation puts Freo in breach from day one where the scheme reserves subrogation rights by statute. This is a compliance trap, not a negotiating position.
flag_if: A waiver of subrogation is required with no carve-out for workers compensation.
A waiver of subrogation is required with no carve-out for compulsory third party motor vehicle cover.
The waiver extends to parties the counterparty may nominate from time to time.
preferred_language: except for compulsory third party motor vehicle insurance and workers compensation insurance, include a waiver of subrogation in favour of the Contractor.

title: Title, risk and PPSA registration
where_to_look: Transfer of risk and title, ownership of equipment, lien and security interest provisions.
required: Freo retains title; the counterparty bears risk in the equipment while in its possession or under its direction; Freo may register its security interest under the PPSA.
fallback: Title retained by Freo, risk with the counterparty, express PPSA registration right, and no counterparty lien over Freo equipment.
escalate_if: Absence of a PPSA clause is a critical gap where any of the fleet is financed - financiers may require it. Escalate.
flag_if: Title in the equipment passes to the counterparty.
Freo bears risk in the equipment while it is in the counterparty's possession or under its direction.
There is no PPSA clause permitting Freo to register its security interest.
The counterparty may claim a lien over Freo's equipment.
Freo is restricted from claiming a lien but the counterparty is not.
There is no counterparty liability for defective servicing or maintenance it performs.
preferred_language: Title in the Equipment remains at all times with the Subcontractor. The Contractor bears the risk of loss of or damage to the Equipment from delivery until collection, except to the extent caused by the negligence of the Subcontractor. The Subcontractor may register its security interest in the Equipment under the Personal Property Securities Act 2009 (Cth), and the Contractor must promptly do all things reasonably required to enable that registration. The Contractor shall not claim or permit any lien or encumbrance over the Equipment.

title: Missing hire-agreement machinery
where_to_look: Run this as a completeness check against any hire arrangement. These are the provisions a hire agreement needs and a services agreement typically omits entirely.
required: A hire arrangement must contain the standard equipment protections. Where the counterparty's paper is a services agreement, these are usually all absent.
fallback: Insert: a responsibilities matrix (consumables, spares, maintenance); inspection reports on delivery and collection; obligations on the counterparty as to how it uses and maintains the equipment, including use only by authorised and qualified personnel; a restriction on modifying or altering the equipment; maintenance and repair obligations; and indemnities in Freo's favour for damage caused by the counterparty's use.
escalate_if: Do not sign a hire arrangement without a delivery/collection condition report - it is the only evidence base for damage claims.
flag_if: There is no responsibilities matrix allocating consumables, spares, servicing and maintenance.
There is no requirement for inspection or condition reports on delivery and collection of equipment.
There are no obligations on the counterparty as to how it uses and maintains the equipment.
There is no requirement that the equipment be operated only by authorised and qualified personnel.
There is no restriction on the counterparty modifying or altering the equipment.
There are no maintenance and repair obligations.
There is no indemnity in Freo's favour for damage caused by the counterparty's use of the equipment.
There are no corporate warranties as to power and authority, and the agreement is not being executed under s 127 of the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth).

title: Plant breakdown and mobilisation thresholds
where_to_look: Plant breakdown, availability, repair and mobilisation-delay provisions, including any thresholds or liquidated sums.
required: Breakdown and mobilisation-delay thresholds must be validated against fleet reality before signature.
fallback: Commercially verified thresholds; root-cause obligations excluded where the cause is a third party.
escalate_if: These are commercial-verification items, not legal positions. They must not be signed off by Legal alone.
flag_if: Breakdown, availability or mobilisation-delay thresholds have not been verified against fleet reality — route to Operations and Commercial.
Root cause analysis is required irrespective of cause.
Repair or replacement timeframes are not achievable.

title: Wind speed thresholds and adverse weather definitions
where_to_look: Wind speed threshold, high wind event, adverse weather condition and weather relief definitions.
required: Wind speed thresholds and adverse weather definitions must match the lift plans and the fleet's operating limits.
fallback: Thresholds confirmed by the technical team against lift plans before signature.
escalate_if: These definitions determine whether weather downtime is paid. They are commercial and technical, not legal.
flag_if: Wind speed thresholds have not been confirmed against the lift plans and fleet operating limits — route to the technical team.
Weather relief requires weather events to persist for more than a stated number of hours in aggregate per day.
Hail or heavy rain qualifies only if it makes the work unsafe or non-compliant.
The weather definition depends on a corresponding definition in the head contract.

title: Intellectual property ownership and licence scope
where_to_look: Intellectual property ownership, assignment and licence provisions, and ownership of drawings, plans and lift plans.
required: Freo retains all IP in its equipment, methods, lift plans and documents. Any licence to the counterparty is limited to the project.
fallback: Licence limited to use for this project only - delete 'or any Project' and similar open-ended grants. Carve out Freo's proprietary information, techniques and documents from any assignment of drawings and plans.
escalate_if: Do not grant a licence permitting use of Freo's engineering or lift-planning IP on other projects.
flag_if: The licence granted to the counterparty extends beyond this project (for example 'or any Project').
Freo's pre-existing IP is not carved out of any assignment.
IP conceived outside the performance of the work is not carved out.
Plans and drawings prepared by Freo become the counterparty's property with no carve-out for proprietary methods.
The licence back is not limited to what is necessary to use the deliverable.
An IP indemnity extends beyond the contracting entity.
preferred_language: Notwithstanding any other provision of this clause, pre-existing Intellectual Property of the Subcontractor, and any other Intellectual Property which the Subcontractor conceives or makes, alone or with others, outside the performance of the Subcontract Work, remains the sole and absolute property of the Subcontractor, and the Contractor obtains no right, title or interest in it. To the extent any such Intellectual Property is incorporated into the Subcontract Work, the Subcontractor grants the Contractor a perpetual, irrevocable, non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to use it, but only to the extent necessary to use the Subcontract Work into which it is incorporated.

title: Confidentiality - mutuality and permitted disclosure
where_to_look: Confidentiality provisions and the permitted disclosure exceptions.
required: Mutual confidentiality obligations, with carve-outs for professional advisers, insurers, financiers and affiliates.
fallback: Mutuality plus a professional-adviser carve-out.
escalate_if: Low risk, but a one-way obligation with no adviser carve-out impedes ordinary business (including obtaining this very advice).
flag_if: The confidentiality obligation binds Freo only.
Professional advisers are not a permitted disclosure exception.
Insurers and financiers are not permitted disclosure exceptions.
Documents must be returned or destroyed 'immediately'.
A confidentiality or privacy indemnity is one-way.

title: Data privacy and personal information
where_to_look: Data privacy, personal information and data protection provisions.
required: Mutual, controller-to-controller obligations limited to compliance with applicable privacy law.
fallback: Compliance obligations accepted, but expressly not tied to any broad indemnity, and any liability limited to direct losses actually incurred.
escalate_if: Never accept privacy obligations backed by an uncapped or broad indemnity. Route to the Marmon risk team rather than negotiating the substance locally.
flag_if: Privacy obligations are backed by a broad or uncapped indemnity.
Privacy liability is not limited to direct losses actually incurred.
The clause references a foreign privacy regime rather than the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) and the Australian Privacy Principles.
Obligations exceed those required by applicable law — route to the Marmon risk team.

title: Term and extension options
where_to_look: Term, duration, commencement and extension option provisions.
required: A defined term with clearly stated extension options exercisable by agreement.
fallback: Express term, express extension mechanic, and rate review on extension (see PAY-03).
escalate_if: An open-ended term with no rate review is a pricing risk.
flag_if: There is no defined term.
Extension options are exercisable unilaterally by the counterparty.
An extension does not trigger the rate review mechanism (see PAY-03).

title: Rebate schemes
where_to_look: Rebate, volume discount and price-reduction-for-volume provisions.
required: No volume rebate. Any rebate must be tied to committed volume.
fallback: Commercial decision.
escalate_if: Route to Commercial - this is a pricing term, not a legal one.
flag_if: Any rebate, volume discount or volume commitment applies — route to Commercial.

title: First right of refusal
where_to_look: Exclusivity, first right of refusal and additional-scope provisions.
required: A first right of refusal on additional crane work at the site.
fallback: Commercial decision.
escalate_if: Upside term rather than a risk term - pursue where the relationship supports it.
flag_if: There is no first right of refusal on additional lifting scope at the site during the term.

title: Assignment and novation by the counterparty
where_to_look: Assignment, novation and transfer provisions applying to the counterparty.
required: No assignment or novation by the counterparty without Freo's consent.
fallback: Transfer only to an entity of equivalent or better financial standing and technical capability.
escalate_if: Manage where the transfer is to a related body corporate or the project principal, which is common and usually bankability-driven.
flag_if: The counterparty may assign or novate without Freo's consent.
There is no requirement that the transferee be of equivalent or better financial standing and technical capability.
Freo must execute transfer documents within 5 business days or less.
Freo's own assignment rights are more restricted than the counterparty's, with no reasonableness qualifier.
preferred_language: A party is not permitted to assign or novate any of its rights and liabilities under this Contract without the other party's written consent, which is not to be unreasonably withheld, and any transferee must be of equivalent or better financial standing and technical capability.

title: Conditional deed of novation - claims status report
where_to_look: Conditional deed of novation, and any claims status report, prior claims or release obligation on novation. Also any tripartite deed obligation.
required: Manage rather than depart, but build the operational capability to comply.
fallback: Accept the mechanic, but ensure the business can itemise and quantify prior claims within the notice window.
escalate_if: Failure to deliver a claims status report extinguishes the ability to pursue the principal for pre-novation claims, and caps the principal's liability at the stated maximum. This is an operational control, not a drafting issue.
flag_if: Freo must deliver a claims status report on novation, and failure extinguishes claims against the principal — this is an operational control, add it to the contract administration checklist rather than departing.
The principal's liability is capped at the maximum amount stated in Freo's own report.
Freo must enter a tripartite deed on terms required by a security trustee, with no reasonableness qualifier.
The principal entities' liability is several rather than joint and several.

title: Dispute resolution and expert determination
where_to_look: Dispute resolution, expert determination and arbitration provisions, including the nominating authority.
required: Escalation to senior representatives, then expert determination or arbitration with a named nominating body.
fallback: Resolution Institute as the nominating authority for expert determination.
escalate_if: Low risk, but check the nominating body and the seat.
flag_if: There is no escalation step to senior representatives before formal proceedings.
The expert determination nominating authority is not the Resolution Institute.
The seat or governing law does not match the site State.
A dispute does not relieve Freo of the obligation to comply with a direction, and there is no interim payment mechanism.

title: Operators are not counterparty employees
where_to_look: Independent contractor, no-employment and labour-hire provisions. Particularly important wherever the counterparty may direct Freo's personnel.
required: Express confirmation that Freo personnel are not employees of the counterparty even where working under its direction on site.
fallback: An express independent-contractor and no-employment clause covering operators specifically.
escalate_if: Important wherever the counterparty directs Freo crews (see TRM-03) - it manages labour-hire, workers compensation and industrial relations exposure.
flag_if: There is no express statement that Freo's operators are not the counterparty's employees.
The counterparty may direct or control Freo's personnel with no employment carve-out.
preferred_language: For the avoidance of doubt, it is expressly agreed and understood that any operator or other Personnel provided by the Subcontractor shall not be, or be deemed to be, an employee of the Contractor even if such person is under the control of the Contractor on site.

title: Compliance regimes - modern slavery, ABC, codes of conduct, procurement policies
where_to_look: Modern slavery, anti-bribery and corruption, supplier codes of conduct, ethics, sanctions and government procurement policy provisions.
required: Accept, subject to review of the incorporated document.
fallback: Accept, but require a copy of every incorporated policy and add a knowledge qualifier to any termination right for a compliance breach.
escalate_if: Do not accept termination for an anti-bribery breach by a subcontractor without a knowledge qualifier.
flag_if: A code of conduct or policy is incorporated by reference and has not been provided — request a copy.
Termination is available for an anti-bribery breach by a subcontractor with no knowledge qualifier.
Modern slavery obligations survive termination (see TRM-08).
A State procurement policy is imported by reference and has not been reviewed.
preferred_language: and the Contractor knew or ought reasonably to have known of such violation

title: Audit rights
where_to_look: Audit rights, records and inspection provisions.
required: No audit right, or one confined to records directly relevant to amounts invoiced.
fallback: Audit permitted within two years following the end of the year in which the invoice was submitted, on reasonable notice, limited to records relevant to the amounts charged.
escalate_if: Do not accept an open-ended audit right, particularly alongside a most-favoured-customer clause — the two combine into a pricing exposure.
flag_if: The audit right has no time limit.
The audit scope extends beyond records relevant to amounts invoiced.
An audit right accompanies a most favoured customer clause without being narrowed to match (see PAY-09).
preferred_language: The Contractor may conduct an audit of the Subcontractor and the Records within two (2) years following the end of the year in which an invoice was submitted under this Contract, on reasonable notice, limited to records relevant to the amounts charged.

title: Governing law and jurisdiction
where_to_look: Governing law and jurisdiction provisions. Check any particulars or schedule item that sets the jurisdiction.
required: Law of the place where the work is performed, with no conflicts-of-laws override.
fallback: Governing law and jurisdiction of the Australian State or Territory in which the site is located.
escalate_if: Do not accept a foreign governing law or a jurisdiction unconnected to the site. Do not accept a conflicts-of-laws provision that could import another law.
flag_if: The governing law is not the Australian State or Territory in which the work is performed.
The governing law is foreign.
A conflicts-of-laws provision could import another law.
The jurisdiction field in the particulars table is blank or inconsistent with the body clause.
preferred_language: This Contract shall be interpreted in accordance with, and shall be governed by, the laws of the State or Territory in which the work is performed, without regard to any conflicts of laws principles that could require application of any other law.

title: Binding Freo to the head contract
where_to_look: Any provision binding Freo to the head contract, prime contract, main contract or TSI contract, and any flow-down of upstream obligations.
required: Do not accept any obligation to be bound by the head contract. Relevant terms to be extracted and appended to the subcontract.
fallback: Bound only to head contract terms expressly set out in a schedule to the subcontract, plus a paramountcy clause providing that the subcontract prevails on any inconsistency.
escalate_if: Two absolute preconditions before accepting any flow-down: Freo must receive a copy of the head contract before execution, and must have negotiated its liability cap. Never accept blind flow-down.
flag_if: Freo is bound by all the terms and conditions of the head contract.
The head contract has not been provided to Freo.
There is no schedule or exhibit listing the specific head contract terms that apply.
There is no paramountcy clause providing that the subcontract prevails on inconsistency.
Freo must not cause the counterparty to breach the head contract.
Freo is deemed to have knowledge of head contract terms it has not seen.
preferred_language: The Subcontractor agrees to be bound by the terms and conditions of the Head Contract only to the extent such terms and conditions are expressly included and set forth in Schedule [X] attached to this Contract. In the event the Head Contract is in conflict with this Contract, this Contract shall prevail and govern.

title: Back-to-back valuation and payment of variations
where_to_look: Back-to-back provisions for the valuation, process or payment of variations and change directives.
required: Delete the back-to-back clause. Freo's entitlement to payment for a variation must not depend on the customer's recovery upstream.
fallback: One-way flow-down only (owner to contractor to Freo). Never accept back-to-back operating in reverse.
escalate_if: If Freo accepts back-to-back risk it must be a recorded commercial decision made with knowledge of the cash-flow consequence, not a drafting concession.
flag_if: Valuation, process or payment of a variation is on a back-to-back basis with the upstream contract.
Freo is entitled to payment only once the counterparty has been approved and paid upstream.
Back-to-back operates in the reverse direction (for variations initiated by Freo).

title: Claims bound by an upstream determination
where_to_look: Provisions binding Freo to a determination made under the head contract, and any associated waiver of claims.
required: Delete the clause entirely. Freo must not be bound by a determination made under a contract to which it is not a party.
fallback: If the customer insists: Freo must be given a copy of the head contract, and every reference making additional compensation contingent on upstream recovery must be deleted.
escalate_if: Never accept a waiver of Freo's claim for compensation or extension of time based on an upstream determination Freo cannot participate in or challenge.
flag_if: Freo is bound by a determination made under the head contract.
Freo waives any claim for compensation or extension of time relating to that determination.
No compensation or extension is provided unless and until received from the owner upstream.
Freo must execute a change order accepting the resultant adjustment.
